findings: The preserved source asks specifically for longest common substring using DP and contains no API, tie-break, Unicode model, input-size or project-history constraints.

The candidate defines the DP as the common suffix ending at each pair of positions, so a match extends the diagonal state and a mismatch resets to zero; this is the required continuity invariant and is explicitly contrasted with longest common subsequence.
The one-dimensional compression updates j from right to left, preserving the prior-row diagonal dependency instead of reading a value overwritten in the current row.
The implementation is a complete compilable Java class, returns both a valid substring and its length, rejects null inputs explicitly and handles empty/no-match/repeated-character cases.
A deterministic direct brute-force oracle agrees with the compressed DP on 3000 generated input pairs, while fixed cases cover boundaries and multiple optimal matches.
The source does not define a tie-break or Unicode code-point model; the candidate states those boundaries rather than silently claiming one universal contract.
No production performance data or personal project experience is fabricated; alternatives such as suffix automata are framed only as possible choices for different scale constraints.
